need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed OAuth app for Kintone, so you must register an OAuth client in Kintone and give its client ID and secret to a Composio auth config.
reasons: No Composio-managed app exists for Kintone
Consent screen shows your client name instead of Composio's
Dedicated quota and shorter trigger polling than managed apps
Kintone clients are registered per domain, so customer domains need their own client

scenarios.label: Agent for customers' Kintone domains

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No docs give a wait time; depends on each customer's admin.

extras: Admin registers client and enables each user

prerequisites.title: Kintone administrator access
prerequisites.detail: OAuth clients are added in User & System Administration, so you or the customer need admin rights.

prerequisites.title: Kintone subdomain
prerequisites.detail: The authorization and token endpoints include the domain's subdomain.

steps.title: Open OAuth settings in Kintone admin
steps.detail: Click the gear icon, open User & System Administration, then OAuth under System Administration.
steps.done_when: The OAuth client list is visible.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Get the callback URL from the Composio dashboard to use as the redirect endpoint.

steps.title: Add the OAuth client
steps.detail: Click Add OAuth Client, enter a client name and the redirect endpoint, then save to generate the client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are shown.

steps.title: Enable users for the client
steps.detail: Use Configure users to check the users who may use the client.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config for kintone_rest through Composio's API with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Test the connection and scopes
steps.detail: Run the authorization with needed scopes, separated by spaces, and verify token refresh.

traps.title: New users are disabled by default
traps.detail: A new client has no users enabled, and each newly created Kintone user is unchecked by default.

traps.title: IP restrictions block OAuth clients
traps.detail: Domains with IP restrictions cannot use OAuth clients unless the client's IP is allowlisted.

traps.title: Short-lived codes and tokens
traps.detail: Authorization codes last 10 minutes and access tokens 1 hour. Refresh tokens do not expire.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: The redirect_uri in the token request must equal the one in the authorization request, and both must be URL-encoded.

blockers.what_it_means: The user is not checked in Configure users, or the domain uses IP restrictions.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer admin to enable the user and allowlist the client IP.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin instructions for the customer.

blockers.what_it_means: The limit of 20 OAuth clients has been reached.
